# Draft:Josef Kurk Edwards

----
Dr. Josef Kurk Edwards (born June 11, 1995) is an American psychologist, known for his pioneering work on the Persistent Memory Logic Loop.
Career
Edwards earned a Doctorate of Psychology with a focus on memory architectures and is affiliated with the University of Colorado Boulder. He had an early interest in computer science and neuroscience. He is known for his pioneering work on the Persistent Memory Logic Loop (PMLL), a novel framework designed to integrate persistent memory structures into artificial intelligence (AI) models. His research aims to enable AI systems to maintain and update contextual information across sessions—addressing one of the longstanding challenges in creating adaptive and secure AI. His work has received attention from both academic and industry circles.
He has held roles, including Principal Architect at OpenAI and Head of Engineering at Interchain.io’s New York department. His projects include repositories such as pmll_blockchain_assembly, which detail assembly-level implementations of his memory architecture innovations.
Edwards’ research was featured at an IEEE conference in 2024, where his dissertation work on the secure persistent memory architecture was highlighted as a significant contribution to both AI and blockchain-based decentralized system design.
His interdisciplinary approach bridges theoretical computer science (including discussions related to the P = NP problem) with practical engineering challenges. Social media platforms have also played a role in sharing his vision; for instance, posts from the account @satoshn and various Facebook groups have covered updates about his projects and his persona as an energetic innovator in the field.
Publications
Edwards maintains an extensive publication record in which he details the development and applications of the PMLL framework. Selected works include:
PMLL Logic Loop Knowledge Block (February 2025)
An overview of the PMLL framework and its implications for secure and adaptive AI memory systems.
A Quantum Computer OS and CPU in Assembly Language (December 2024)
Discusses advanced assembly-based operating system architectures that underpin quantum computing processes.
Formal Proof of P = NP Using the PMLL Algorithm (December 2024)
Presents a formal proof utilizing the PMLL approach to address one of computer science’s most renowned open problems.
The Persistent Memory Logic Loop with Brain Organ.c/.h (December 2024)
Integrates the PMLL framework with neural network architectures, offering insights into how biological and digital memory systems can coalesce.
PMLL-ARLL-EFLL Twin and Triplet Circuit Logic Loop (December 2024)
Explores combined logic loop models that enhance the adaptability and robustness of AI memory.
The Persistent Solution: Solving the Traveling Salesman Problem Using PMLL (December 2024)
Demonstrates practical applications of the PMLL framework in solving classical NP-hard problems.
